title: Entering a group dims the layer list but not the canvas
detail: SPLIT, and the two halves went opposite ways. The canvas half STAYS OPEN as a decision, not a bug: the dim was declined because opacity is in Fabric stateProperties, so dimming the canvas would serialise view state into every save, which §67 forbids. That reasoning still holds and nothing here overturns it. The layer half was not a decision at all but a defect, and it was worse than this row says — the row recorded that the list dims today (data-context=false), which is true only after something unrelated re-projects the tree. Fixed as vg-058.

title: The line chart occasionally slides left as if correcting a position
detail: NOT REPRODUCED in 30 seconds of live playback against a real host, and BOTH of the rows named candidates are ruled out for that window. The row guessed a resize observer re-fitting mid-animation, or a chart settling after a viewport change; neither fired: the viewport transform was byte-identical at the start and the end (0.61602870 with the same offset, zero changes in thirty samples), the chart own box never moved (left 616, top 695, 963x215, angle 0, scale 1 and 1), and a ResizeObserver on the body fired once, which is the probe own DOM reads rather than anything the chart did. STILL OPEN, because occasionally is rarer than thirty seconds and closing it on a non-reproduction would be the same mistake as filing it on a screenshot. WHAT THE NEXT ATTEMPT SHOULD USE, because two attempts here failed for one reason and the reason is worth keeping: counting ink in the chart region cannot see this. The card is opaque and the sampled rect includes the dark part of the backdrop, so every column reads as drawn and every column reads as dark — the first probe reported a constant firstX of 0 and lastX of the full width, and a luminance profile reported the same. Watching the EVENTS is what separates a slide from data changing, because data moves locally and a slide moves everything.

title: The preview data source fluctuates faster than a real PC
detail: "The Preview data source fluctuate too rapidly which is not realistic to a normal PC hardware behavior, and a bit distracting for the author." The cadence is a number in fake-source. 'Realistic' needs a decision about what the preview is for.

title: The top bar becomes a toolbar of icon buttons on the theme document, and its commands are renamed
detail: "The top bar menu is kinda lost in direction of what's it for. Some are legitimate functions you can't find anywhere else (File & View menus), but Edit & Insert is a duplication of actions that already in their rightful places. Verdict: Make it an actual toolbar (icon buttons, not nested inside a menu) with actions to the theme document, not individual elements." AND the rename, in full: Save Package -> Activate (instructs the player to switch to this theme); Release Package -> Export theme; Open Package -> Import theme; Open library -> Open; Save to library -> Save; ADD a Save as button; New from starter -> New from template (only one template today, more are coming). Note Activate and Save as are missing capabilities, not renames: the host already stores the active theme and the theme route is a PUT to a named id, so each is one id away. Do this as one change, not seven renamings — the Arrange menu was already removed on exactly this reasoning (vg-016), and doing the buttons without the toolbar shape means doing the work twice.

title: Should the editor be rebuilt on Base UI + shadcn/ui + Tailwind before further micro-adjustments?
detail: "Honestly the entire editor UI is kind of boring, primitive & unpolish... Should we do a whole redesign of it with Base UI - Shadcn - TailwindCSS, which has been in the queue long enough, before doing any micro adjustments to specific UI details? I'm talking about the whole panels rearrangement, too." The same question as vg-031 one level up, and the same wrong answer: the ecosystem search was run against Base UI alone. FIRST STEP IS NOT A REDESIGN — it is searching shadcn/ui for the panels this editor already has (dialog, select, tabs, popover, tooltip, slider, switch, scroll-area, separator) and finding out which replace hand-rolled equivalents. Then bring the result back to choose: full redesign first, or defect fixes first. Bigger than any other item here and deliberately unstarted.

title: A desktop-shaped theme letterboxes to 31% of a phone's height
detail: MEASURED: the stress fixture at 412x839 gives an artboard of about 412x258 with bars above and below. Nothing overflows, nothing is cropped, no console errors — this is contain working exactly as §53 specifies. Filed because two rulings pull against each other and only the user can settle which wins: "a phone is the main display type" and "content is always contain" cannot both be satisfied by a desktop-shaped theme on a portrait phone, because the content will be whole and the text about 6px. Three ways out — leave it, add a per-display fit, or let a theme declare the size it is designed for — and which one is right depends on who reads these displays and from how far.

title: The line chart's Glass control: a Circle's frost reads stronger than a Rect's at the same value
detail: RULING STANDS: a slight per-shape difference is acceptable rather than no glass on closed shapes; the expensive option wins by default. CHARACTERISED, NOT FIXED, and the lead I gave the investigator was wrong. I offered "the Circle region measured 127,449 px against the Rect 156,009 for the same box" as proof the region was shape-dependent. It is not: that sweep gave every shape the same AUTHORING box, and a Circle has no 240x160. Both numbers reconstruct exactly at the sweep pad — 437x357 = 156,009 and 357x357 = 127,449, predicted ratio 0.8165 against 0.81691 measured. At one 260x260 box all five shapes take a byte-identical 362x362 region (131,044 px). PARTIAL COVERAGE REFUTED: no collapse at the rim, and the bin touching the boundary is the largest bin in three of four measurements. MATERIAL PARITY IS BIT-IDENTICAL: mean luma 94.75/94.75 over stripes and 93.41/93.41 over a photograph, distinct colours 40/40 and 10/10, and the frost boxes are pixel-identical at thresholds 2, 1.5 and 1. WHAT DIFFERS IS FOOTPRINT: a Circle covers 78.54% of its box, 21.5% less frosted area — which reads LIGHTER, not stronger, so it is the wrong direction to explain the report. STILL OPEN, and the leading hypothesis is not the renderer: a Circle authored size is a RADIUS and a Rect authored size is a WIDTH, so the same number gives a disc twice the area. Checked and not yet confirmed in the scene where it was seen. glass.ts is byte-identical to the base sha; nothing was simulated away, per the ruling. THE AUTHORS PATH TO THIS COMPARISON IS REACHABLE AFTER ALL, and I said otherwise earlier and was wrong twice about it. First: I claimed the Glass blur control does not exist on a chart. It does not exist on a chart because a chart cannot be frosted — the control appears once there is a radius to tune, and I compared an object that was refused against one that already had frost on. Second: I then said the report could not have come from the editor because the line charts control cannot be changed. True, and beside the point: the report is about a CIRCLE and a RECT, and both are perfectly authorable. MEASURED ACROSS EVERY SHAPE, which is also the ruling ADR-0015 predicts: Rect, Circle, Ellipse, Triangle and Polygon all offer an ENABLED Frosted glass control; Polyline and Line are aria-disabled, correctly, having no closed area to frost. And the two shapes the report names get the SAME DEFAULT: a fresh Circle and a fresh Rectangle both become vigiliaGlass at blurRadius 16 the moment frost is switched on, with the blur control appearing alongside it. So the situation the report describes — a Circle and a Rect at the same value — is exactly what the product produces by default, and the row stands on its own merits again. What remains is what the earlier characterisation established and this does not change: over the area they share the frost is bit-identical, and what differs is footprint, a Circle covering 78.54 percent of its box. If a Circle reads stronger, the leading hypothesis is still the authors own — a Circle size is a RADIUS where a Rectangle size is a WIDTH — and it is still unconfirmed in the scene where it was seen.
check: Measured across every shape in the running editor: Frosted glass is enabled on Rect, Circle, Ellipse, Triangle and Polygon, and aria-disabled on Polyline and Line with the reason on focus. A fresh Circle and a fresh Rectangle both take blurRadius 16 on the same click, and the Glass blur control appears only after that.

title: Auto-save, and a prompt for recovery after a browser crash
detail: RULED: draft in browser storage; write on a ~30 s timer and on leaving the page; recovery offers restore-or-discard naming what was lost; and the editor opens a theme from the library, which is the seam the other two need. BLOCKED: the asset-ownership question decides where the draft lives — if the editor stops holding asset bytes and the host owns them, the draft is a host write and browser storage is wrong.

title: What is derived state in a persisted Fabric object?
detail: The dirty guard's cause (vg-026) is one field of a general question, and patching styles alone leaves the next per-character cache to arrive and be found by the user. SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES is an allowlist that already intends to do this job and is not applied on the way out. The spec should answer which Fabric properties are derived from telemetry or from rendering, how a serialisation excludes all of them, and whether the allowlist should be enforced at the boundary. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-30-asset-ownership.md. AND NOW THERE IS A SHARP INSTANCE OF IT, MEASURED, which is vg-026. The dirty guard compares a document key against one captured when the editor was built, and with no input at all 13 of the Starter 52 objects change between 0.4 and 1.9 seconds after load — every one a Textbox, repainted by the live preview pass. The document differs from itself with nothing touched, so every New asks the author to save work nobody did. That is what the allowlist was meant to stop and does not reach: the changed objects are bound text, and what the live pass writes is the same property the author edits. This row is therefore not an abstract design question any more — it is one concrete false prompt an author meets on the first Ctrl+N, and the fix belongs here rather than in the dirty guard.

title: The artboard is not a clipping area, and neither repair is free
detail: Fabric has no scene-level clip: clipPath is per-object and serialised through cacheProperties, so it collides with the crop manager's authored per-image clip and with the derived text-box clip. Two candidate repairs, both with consequences — a scene Group wrapper changes what canvas.getObjects() means, which is the layer tree's and every walk over it. A decision, not a patch. Related: a selection handle should stay fully visible when its object is clipped (the user's own requirement in the same report).

title: Where the defect queue lives: the open-ended pass, the Superpowers lifecycle, and beads
detail: The working-out of whether every defect should become a spec and a plan (overkill), and where an open-ended queue sits beside a change lifecycle that has a finish line. Beads is proven installable natively on Windows (v1.3.0, no WSL) with the full lifecycle exercised; bd init edits AGENTS.md and installs hooks by default and --skip-agents declines that. Marked undecided by the user pending thought — specifically, not wanting two agent frameworks fighting each other. The registry is the incumbent until this is decided.

title: The layer list cannot select more than one row, and grouping needs a multi-selection
detail: The row click is onClick={() => selectLayer(row.id)} and ignores the event, so a shift-click on a second row replaces the first instead of adding to it. MEASURED: shift-clicking strapline after wordmark left only strapline selected, while the same two objects shift-clicked on the canvas select both. Grouping is reachable — the context menu offers Group once the selection is eligible — but only from a canvas multi-selection, so an author working in the layer list cannot make one. Needs a decision rather than a patch: whether a shift-click toggles a row the way the canvas does, whether shift extends a range like a file list, or whether the panel stays single-select and grouping moves somewhere reachable from it. An additive select also has to cross the Fabric-free bridge, which has one selectLayer(id) today.

title: Reopening the editor discards saved work and shows the Starter instead
detail: MEASURED THREE WAYS, and it is the second half of vg-059's damage. Rename the theme through the theme-settings Name field from System dashboard to SENTINEL-9931 - the field reads SENTINEL-9931 and the host's document reads {"name":"SENTINEL-9931"}. Then reload the editor page. The Name field reads System dashboard again and the layer list is the Starter's 52 rows. The saved work is still on the host - it is the editor that does not open it. So the author's round trip is: edit, see it saved, close the tab, reopen, and be holding the Starter with no prompt and no warning that what they were working on is still there. NOT THE SAME AS vg-026: that row is the discard prompt appearing when it should not, and this is a document that never being loaded in the first place, so even discarding everything correctly would not help. THE ACTIVE THEME IS UNSET, which is where I would look first but have not established: /api/themes/active returns {"active":null} alongside the theme list, so nothing designates vigilia-demo-dashboard as what the editor should open, and Save to library evidently does not set it. Save to library, Release package and Open package are three different verbs in the File menu and only one of them is the one an author means by save. Worth noting for whoever picks this up: the editor does reach the library through File > Open library, so the path exists - what is missing is that the default open is the Starter rather than the author's own theme, and that Open library first raises the same spurious Save changes before opening another theme prompt that vg-026 is about.

title: Insert > Text takes the caret, so the first keystroke lands
detail: FIXED, and the obvious fix was not the one that worked. insertNewText now enters editing and selects the new text, which is what every editor this product is measured against does when you ask for a text box. Calling it SYNCHRONOUSLY put the caret in and then lost it: the menu the insert came from takes focus back for itself as it closes, so a keystroke after Insert still went nowhere and document.activeElement was BODY. The call is deferred a frame, and guarded on the new object still being the active one so a late frame does not steal focus from whatever the author has moved on to. EditorInteraction.textManager.addText was widened to FabricObject although the manager has always returned a Textbox and its own interface said so; narrowing it there is what lets a caller enter editing at all. TWO TEST-STUB FIXES were needed and are worth naming because both would have passed for the wrong reason: the panel stub returned undefined from getActiveObject, so the guard could never pass; and addText was typed to return undefined, which is not what it returns.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor: after Insert > Text the focused element is a TEXTAREA (Fabric hidden textarea) with isEditing true, and typing Hello leaves the object reading Hello — where it previously stayed New text. Red without the call: the new test fails. Editor suite 1054 across 85 files.

title: The editor never says an object has fallen outside the artboard, but the player counts them precisely
detail: MEASURED AS A CONTRAST BETWEEN THE TWO SURFACES, which is what makes it a defect rather than a missing nicety. In the editor, type 700 into the theme-settings Width field and 400 into Height - the canvas zooms to 199% and 44 of the 52 objects are now outside the artboard. The editor says nothing. Its entire off-artboard vocabulary is one static sentence that is present at every size and never changes: Objects are not moved or resized. Anything outside the artboard is not shown on a display. No count, no badge, no highlighted layer row, no status-bar line, and /outside|off.?canvas|clipped/i matches exactly that one sentence. Save to library and open the player on the same document, and it says: 44 of 52 objects are outside this artboard and are not shown - past the right edge and past the bottom edge. Same document, same host, same numbers, and the surface an author can act in is the silent one. The direction is the part that should be hard to reproduce by accident: naming the right edge and the bottom edge means the player already computes which side each object fell off, and that per-object answer is exactly what an author needs to fix the layout. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING. The editor is where the mistake is made and the only place it can be undone, and it is the one surface that does not know the mistake happened. Worth noting the player earns its keep here - this is not a case for adding a warning to a display, it is a case for the author not having to go and look at a display to find out. The count and the edge names are already computed; nothing new needs deciding about how to say it, only where to say it.

title: Release package and Open package do nothing at all, beside a Save package that works
detail: MEASURED AS A COMPARISON, because the sibling command proves the plumbing is there and the shell is not the problem. Click File > Save package: a download fires, vigilia-demo-dashboard.vigilia-theme. Click File > Release package: no dialog, no download, no toast, no status-bar text, no page error, and the editor is byte-identical afterwards - the status bar still reads Fabric editor ready. Click File > Open package: exactly the same nothing. So of the three verbs an author is given to move a theme between the editor and the rest of the world, one works and two are inert, and the two inert ones are the two that would be the export and the import - the operations that make a theme portable at all. A prior note in the register recorded Release package prompting for a version bump and Save package not downloading in that state; NEITHER half reproduces now, so that observation is superseded rather than confirmed: there is no prompt and there is no failure, there is no handler. The Release version field is present and empty in the theme-settings panel, which is a second loose end: an author is shown a version input for a command that never asks them for it. Worth noting this is exactly the rename vg-034 already proposes - Release package becomes Export theme and Open package becomes Import theme - so the naming decision and the missing capability are one piece of work, not two, and renaming a button that does nothing would be worse than leaving it.

title: Opening Assets or Settings throws away the layer list's scroll position
detail: MEASURED, AND THE SELECTION SURVIVING IS WHAT MAKES IT WORTH FILING. Scroll the layer list down through the Starter's 52 rows to the VRAM block - scrollTop 499, showing vram-value, vram-gauge, vram-card-title, vram-card-icon. Click the Assets icon in the left rail, then click Layers again. The list is back at scrollTop 0, showing network-chart, network-up, network-down, network-card-title: the top of the list, exactly where it started. The selection does NOT reset - trends-card-title stayed selected across the same round trip, the inspector kept its geometry, and the canvas kept its handles - so this is not a re-render that throws state away wholesale, it is the scroll offset alone. THE RAIL IS SINGLE-PANEL, which is the design fact underneath it: opening Assets sets the Layers button to aria-pressed=false and Show Layers, so the two cannot be open together and the switch is a real teardown. With 52 objects in the Starter and more in a theme an author has built, finding your place again after a glance at the assets is the whole cost. Cheap to confirm and cheap to keep: hold the scroll offset across the panel swap.

title: Renaming a bound object saves a document with a dangling binding, and nothing says so
detail: THE SAME DEFECT AS vg-059 REACHED BY A DIFFERENT ROUTE, AND IT IS WORSE IN ONE RESPECT. Rename rather than delete: focus the network-down row, press Enter, type RENAMED-BOUND, press Enter, then File > Save to library. The save SUCCEEDS - the host's document reads 52 objects, network-down is gone, RENAMED-BOUND is there - and the document now carries a dangling binding, which I can read directly off it: bindings still has a network-down key while no scene object has that name. So the two paths through the same cause end differently. Deleting throws, the save silently aborts, and nothing is written. Renaming writes the broken document and reports success. The author is left with a theme whose stored bindings no longer match its stored scene, and the only evidence is a key in a JSON file they never see. THE PLAYER IS FINE WITH IT, which is worth recording so nobody chases the wrong end: opening that document in the player renders it, one canvas, only the LibreHardwareMonitor strip, no error. So the corruption is invisible on every surface the product shows an author - it is only visible in the file. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A COSMETIC ONE: the bindings are keyed by object NAME (established in vg-059 - the document's bindings map has 25 keys that are object names), so renaming is a rename of a key an author cannot see. The inspector offers no warning that the object is bound and no indication that renaming will detach its telemetry, and there is no list anywhere in the UI of which objects are bound. Renaming a bound object should either carry its binding with it or refuse, and if it is allowed at all the author should be told what just stopped updating. The keyboard rename path is otherwise good - Enter opens the field, the edit lands, the list re-renders - so the fix belongs at the rename, not at the key handling. RE-VERIFIED AFTER THE vg-059 FIX, AND THIS ROW IS NOT FIXED BY IT. The delete-side fix landed as 8bff539 (a binding no longer outlives the object it names) and I re-ran both halves by hand against a rebuilt bundle. DELETE: fixed - selecting network-up, pressing Delete and saving now takes the document 52 to 51, leaves dangling: [], throws no pageerror, and an unrelated rename typed immediately afterwards lands as POST-FIX-CHECK. RENAME: still broken - focusing the network-down row, pressing Enter, typing RENAMED-BOUND-2 and saving gives count 52, hasOld false, hasNew true and dangling: ["network-down"], with no error of any kind. So the fix covers the path that deletes an object and not the path that renames one, which is the more reachable of the two: renaming is a two-key action an author does while tidying names, and it is the one that writes the broken document rather than refusing it. The repair is almost certainly the same rule applied at the rename rather than a second rule - a binding names an object, so a rename has to carry the key or drop the binding, and the error case should be told to the author either way.

title: The layer list declares role=treeitem but answers to none of a tree's keys
detail: MEASURED KEY BY KEY, and the gap between what the panel promises and what it does is the whole finding. Each row is a div with role=treeitem, tabindex=0 and an aria-selected attribute, and the rows are genuinely reachable by Tab - a 45-step walk found 12 treeitems in the tab order, so this is not a keyboard-inaccessible panel. But with a row focused, none of the keys a tree is defined by do anything. Focus network-down and press ArrowDown twice, ArrowUp, ArrowRight, Home and End in turn: focus stays on network-down for all six, and aria-selected stays false. Space does nothing at all - focus unchanged, inspector unchanged, zero rows report aria-selected=true anywhere in the list. Enter is the one key that responds, and it responds by opening a rename input, not by selecting: after Enter the active element is an INPUT holding network-down and the inspector still reads None. So the panel announces itself as a tree, is tab-reachable as a tree, and then implements neither roving focus, nor arrow navigation, nor selection - only rename. Escape from that rename drops focus to BODY, which loses the author's place in the tab order entirely. There is a second cost beyond the keyboard: a screen reader announces a tree with its expand/collapse and level semantics, so it promises structure that is not there and cannot be discovered by touch either. Worth saying plainly what is NOT wrong: selection by click works, the row exposes aria-selected, and the rename flow is a real feature. This is a mismatch between a declared role and a delivered one, and either the role or the keys have to change - a tree that only renames is a list.

title: Hiding a panel widens the canvas but the theme does not refit, so the freed space is wasted
detail: MEASURED ACROSS FIVE WINDOW WIDTHS, and the numbers make the case better than the complaint would. Both side panels are fixed at 280 px, so the canvas takes what is left: at 2048 the canvas is 1394 wide at 72% zoom, at 1600 it is 946 at 57%, at 1440 it is 786 at 47%, at 1280 it is 626 at 37%, and at 1024 it is 370 at 22% - 36% of the window. A 1024-wide window is a half-screen window on an ordinary laptop, not a phone, and the theme is unreadable there. THE PART THAT MAKES IT A DEFECT RATHER THAN A DIMENSION IS THE COLLAPSE. The layer panel has a Hide button in the rail. Click it at 1024 and the canvas goes from 370 to 658 - it nearly doubles - and the zoom stays at exactly 22%. The screenshot is the evidence: the artboard sits at the left of a 658-wide canvas with several hundred pixels of black to its right, unchanged in size. So the author is given the exact control that would fix the problem, the space is demonstrably freed, and the viewport is not recomputed to use it. Nothing tells them either: the zoom badge still reads 22% and no hint appears. CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST PASS, because I nearly filed a wrong cause: the View menu does offer only Data source, Chart refresh and Value runs, which made me think the zoom commands were unreachable. They are not. The zoom badge in the bottom-right of the canvas is a button with aria-label Zoom level, and opening it gives exactly the three commands an author would reach for - Zoom to fit, Zoom to selection and 100 %. So the controls exist and are reachable in one click, which makes this narrower and sharper: Zoom to fit is the command that would consume the freed width, the author has it, and nothing invokes it when the canvas resizes. The defect is the missing refit on resize, not a missing control - and the test for it is simply whether hiding the panel leaves the same 22% that Zoom to fit would change. The panels are also not collapsible on the right: the only rail toggles are Show/Hide Layers, Add, Assets and Settings, and there is no control for the 280 px inspector, which is the panel that would have to give for the canvas to grow on the right. WIDER THAN THE PANEL CASE, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. It is not only hiding a panel - the zoom never refits when the window itself is resized. Start at 1440 and the zoom badge reads 47%. Drag the window to 1800 and the canvas goes 786 to 1146 with the zoom still exactly 47%. Drag it to 2048 and the canvas is 1394, still 47%. Drag it back down to 1100 and the canvas collapses to 446, still 47%. One number across a 946-pixel change in available width. Click Zoom to fit at the last size and it drops to 27%, which is the correct fit for 446 - so the fit calculation is right and simply is not being run. The consequence for an author is that the zoom they set once is the zoom they keep for the rest of the session, and it was computed against whatever the window happened to be when they opened the editor. On the machine I was given, opening at the maximized 2048 gives 72% and every narrower window after that is stuck at 72%, so opening on a small window and maximising leaves the theme stranded small in a large black field. A canvas editor that does not refit its viewport on resize is a category of defect every editor in this category solved years ago, and here the whole mechanism is already written - it is the Zoom to fit command and a resize listener.
